title: Dominic and the Oath
premise: Wren Galloway has hidden for twelve years as a charm-seller in the city of Corvane, where magic is outlawed and his own gatekeeping oath binds him to a sealed border. When the wards collapse on the night the stars vanish, Wren learns the court beneath the mountain bought the soul of Tam, the found-family apprentice who is all he has left, as payment to keep the sky dark and their power absolute. To save Tam, Wren must break his own oath, gather a ragged company of outlaws, exiles, and one repentant warden, and descend into the mountain court where justice is a currency only the desperate can afford. In the end, Wren discovers he cannot steal Tam's soul back—he can only offer his own in trade—and by surrendering the identity of 'keeper' that defined him, he shatters the court's claim, relights the stars, and builds a new family from the broken people who walked down with him.
about_author: Noor Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing outlawed folk charms before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about quiet people forced into loud rebellions, and live somewhere near a border they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Wren sells a luck-knot to a frightened fisherman, hiding his true gift behind harmless trinkets. POV: Wren. Establishes his careful invisibility, his bond with apprentice Tam, and the daily fear of the Wardens' patrols. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built on smallness.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Shut Doors
chapters.summary: Flashback through Wren's memory: the night he swore the keeper's oath at the border gate and sealed away both the magic beyond it and his old name. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief disguised as duty; we learn what the oath cost him.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam confesses she's been visiting a broker who promises to restore her family's stolen land—paid in something she won't name. Wren forbids it; Tam storms out. POV: alternating Wren/Tam. Emotional beat: first fracture in their found family.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every star over Corvane goes dark at once, and the border wards fall like cut ropes. Panic floods the city; Wardens begin burning charm-shops. Wren feels his oath snap inside his chest. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror and terrible freedom.

chapters.title: Ashes on Copper Lane
chapters.summary: Wren finds his shop raided and Tam gone—taken by hooded figures toward the mountain. A dying broker gasps that her soul was 'collected as payment.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt ignites into resolve; the quest begins.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Looked Away
chapters.summary: Wren blackmails Serah Vail, a Warden who once ignored his illegal charms, into guiding him past checkpoints. She agrees—for reasons she keeps sealed. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Road of Hanged Kings
chapters.summary: On the outlaw road they meet Brannoc, a giant exiled for healing soldiers, who joins them after Wren mends a curse no one else could touch. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: the found family gains its first stranger-turned-kin.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: A river spirit demands a memory as toll. Wren pays with the face of his pre-oath self, deepening his identity crisis. Serah witnesses his sacrifice and softens. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the cost of the road made flesh.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: They reach the mountain's mouth, where petitioners queue for centuries seeking justice from the Undercourt. Wren learns its law: souls may be traded, but never stolen back—only exchanged. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: dread of a system built to be unwinnable.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Inside, clerk-magistrate Ivo shows Wren the ledger: Tam's soul was purchased to fuel the starless sky. The court offers Wren a deal—betray his companions and walk free. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Prison of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Wren finds Tam in the soul-vaults, hollow-eyed, unable to remember him. He realizes memory, not just soul, was taken. POV: Tam (fragmented). Emotional beat: heartbreak—the person saved may not remember being loved.

chapters.title: Serah's Oath-Breaking
chapters.summary: Serah reveals why she came: the court holds her sister's soul too, and she has served them hoping to buy it back. She chooses rebellion instead. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: a loyal soldier burns her own badge.

chapters.title: The Vault of Unlit Things
chapters.summary: The company infiltrates the vaults during the court's Long Reckoning. Brannoc holds the door; Wren reaches Tam's vessel—but touching it triggers an alarm woven into his own old oath. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: hope ambushed by betrayal from within himself.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Pale Bench
chapters.summary: Captured, Wren stands trial before the Undercourt, which claims his keeper's oath makes him complicit in every sealed injustice. He argues that justice outside the law is still justice. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: defiance as identity re-forged.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: The court offers the exchange: a soul for a soul. Wren secretly prepares to give his own, lying to his companions about the plan. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love expressed as deception; the loner reverting to old habits.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Door
chapters.summary: Brannoc, presumed lost holding the vault door, returns having freed the queued petitioners—a mob of the wronged now floods the court demanding their hearings. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: the oppressed become the storm.

chapters.title: Ivo's Ledger Burns
chapters.summary: Clerk Ivo, moved by centuries of recorded grief, turns witness against the court and reads the ledger aloud, unmaking its legal claims one entry at a time. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: complicity redeemed through truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: At the altar, Wren offers his soul—but because he paid the river his old self, the court cannot bind what has no fixed name, and the contract collapses. Tam's soul tears free. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the climax—identity itself as the weapon.

chapters.title: When the Stars Came Back
chapters.summary: The court crumbles as its stolen light escapes; stars reignite over Corvane. Wren, half-drained, carries Tam out as the mountain exhales twelve years of dark. POV: Serah. Emotional beat: awe after ruin; dawn as verdict.

chapters.title: Names We Choose
chapters.summary: Recovering in a waystation, Tam slowly regains memories—not the old ones, but new ones being made. Wren stops mourning his erased past and introduces himself, truly, for the first time. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt from chosen bonds.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Open
chapters.summary: Wren returns to the border gate and, instead of resealing it, becomes keeper of an open crossing—warding it fairly rather than shutting it absolutely. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the theme resolved; guardianship without imprisonment.

chapters.title: Charms for the Road Ahead
chapters.summary: Epilogue: the found family opens a shop together—honest magic, fair prices, a bell that rings for anyone seeking justice. Tam hangs the first charm: a small tin star. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: home, finally, with the door unlocked.
